e-15602.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15602.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/a664a3af1ba466491d209dadd32a3be026a5179ac2d0281b55f30917f9ab016b.png)
What would be the vector equation of the line?
e-15602.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+2t \\ 5t \\ 1-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 5t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

e-15603.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15603.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/a4c6f7b2422f1515e1708bf1641dcbec57eeb2d85e4ac03bd98668db34088afc.png)
Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
e-15603.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-t \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,3,1)$ and is parallel to the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041770/assets/11701a2d63851a3f241d8bd905693abaaa6eda6fe4ba0c5710c92d8189595ffd.png)

Question 1
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=2+4ty=34−2tz=3+t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[2142]+t[−421],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[2343]+t[4−21],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[3342]+t[1−24],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[3342]+t[−241],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[5343]+t[42−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Collect the constant terms into the position vector (2, 3/4, 3) and the coefficients of t into the direction vector (4, -2, 1). This gives option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+4t \\ y=\frac{3}{4}-2t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+4t \\ \frac{3}{4}-2t \\ 3+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+4t \\ y=\frac{3}{4}-2t \\ z=3+t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+4t \\ \frac{3}{4}-2t \\ 3+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{4} \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

decision.explanation: The constant terms give the position vector (5, -2, 0), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (-9, 7, -8). Therefore the vector equation is option b.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-9t \\ y=-2+7t \\ z=-8t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-9t \\ -2+7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9t \\ 7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5−9ty=−2+7tz=−8t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[520]+t[9−7−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[5−20]+t[−97−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[5−20]+t[978],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[52−8]+t[−970],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[520]+t[978],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

These parametric equations are equivalent to [xyz]=[5−9t−2+7t−8t][xyz]=[5−20]+[−9t7t−8t][xyz]=[5−20]+t[−97−8]r=[5−20]+t[−97−8], where t∈(−∞,∞).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option b: the constants form (5, -2, 0), and the coefficients of t form (-9, 7, -8). Expanding this vector equation reproduces all three parametric equations. The deliberately submitted option c has incorrect signs.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-9t \\ y=-2+7t \\ z=-8t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-9t \\ -2+7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-9t \\ 7t \\ -8t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 7 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 3
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=1−5ty=2+tz=t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
 r=[−511]+t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 None of the listed
c
 r=t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[120]+t[−511],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
 r=t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constants give the position vector (1, 2, 0), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (-5, 1, 1). Their sum gives option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-5t \\ y=2+t \\ z=t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-5t \\ 2+t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

EXPLANATION

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1-5t \\ y=2+t \\ z=t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-5t \\ 2+t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5t \\ t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 4
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=4ty=−2tz=−3 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[00−3]+t[−240],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
 None of the listed
c
r=[003]+t[420],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[00−3]+t[4−20],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=t[4−2−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms form (0, 0, -3), and the coefficients of t form (4, -2, 0). Thus option d reproduces x=4t, y=-2t, and z=-3.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4t \\ y=-2t \\ z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=4t \\ y=-2t \\ z=-3\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 5
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=11y=3+7tz=−5t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[11−30]+t[057],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[11−30]+t[075],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[−1130]+t[075],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[1103]+t[−570],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[1130]+t[07−5],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constants form the position vector (11, 3, 0), and the coefficients of t form the direction vector (0, 7, -5). This matches option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=11 \\ y=3+7t \\ z=-5t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3+7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=11 \\ y=3+7t \\ z=-5t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3+7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7t \\ -5t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 7 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-4t \\ y=-7+3t \\ z=9-t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-4t \\ -7+3t \\ 9-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4t \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,-7,9)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5-4t \\ y=-7+3t \\ z=9-t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-4t \\ -7+3t \\ 9-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4t \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -7 \\ 9\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,-7,9)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5t-7 \\ y=-1-10t \\ z=\frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5t-7 \\ -1-10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t+\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ -10t \\ \frac{1}{4}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ -1 \\ \frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-7,-1,\frac{3}{5})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].$
